cards.front: Which kidney structures come from the ureteric bud, and which come from the metanephric mesenchyme?
cards.back: **Ureteric bud** (an outgrowth of the mesonephric duct): ureter, renal pelvis, calyces and **collecting ducts**. **Metanephric mesenchyme**: the nephron, from **Bowman capsule** to the **distal convoluted tubule**. Each tissue induces the other to develop.
cards.back_pt: **Broto ureteral** (projeção do ducto mesonéfrico): ureter, pelve renal, cálices e **ductos coletores**. **Mesênquima metanéfrico**: o néfron, da **cápsula de Bowman** até o **túbulo contorcido distal**. Cada tecido induz o desenvolvimento do outro.

cards.front: What causes multicystic dysplastic kidney, and what is its usual course?
cards.back: Abnormal interaction between the **ureteric bud** and the **metanephric mesenchyme** leaves a nonfunctional kidney made of **cysts** and connective tissue. It is usually **unilateral**, and the other kidney compensates. Bilateral disease causes **Potter sequence**.
cards.back_pt: A interação anormal entre o **broto ureteral** e o **mesênquima metanéfrico** gera um rim sem função, formado por **cistos** e tecido conjuntivo. Em geral é **unilateral**, e o outro rim compensa. A doença bilateral causa **sequência de Potter**.

cards.front: Which problems is a horseshoe kidney prone to?
cards.back: The fused **lower poles** distort the course of the ureters and slow drainage. This raises the risk of **hydronephrosis** (often from **UPJ obstruction**), **kidney stones** and **urinary infection**. Some renal tumors, including **Wilms tumor**, are also more common.
cards.back_pt: Os **polos inferiores** fundidos alteram o trajeto dos ureteres e retardam a drenagem. Isso aumenta o risco de **hidronefrose** (frequentemente por **obstrução da JUP**), **litíase renal** e **infecção urinária**. Alguns tumores renais, incluindo o **tumor de Wilms**, também são mais comuns.

cards.front: Where are the three natural narrowings of the ureter?
cards.back: 1) The **ureteropelvic junction** (UPJ). 2) The point where the ureter **crosses the iliac vessels** at the pelvic brim. 3) The **ureterovesical junction** (UVJ), where the ureter passes through the bladder wall. Stones tend to get stuck at these sites.
cards.back_pt: 1) A **junção ureteropélvica** (JUP). 2) O ponto em que o ureter **cruza os vasos ilíacos** na borda da pelve. 3) A **junção ureterovesical** (JUV), onde o ureter atravessa a parede da bexiga. Os cálculos tendem a ficar presos nesses pontos.

cards.front: What does 'water under the bridge' mean in pelvic anatomy, and why does it matter in surgery?
cards.back: The **ureter** (water) runs **under** the **uterine artery** in women and under the **ductus deferens** in men (the bridge). During a **hysterectomy**, the ureter can be tied or cut by mistake when the uterine artery is ligated.
cards.back_pt: O **ureter** (a água) passa **por baixo** da **artéria uterina** na mulher e do **ducto deferente** no homem (a ponte; *water under the bridge*). Na **histerectomia**, o ureter pode ser ligado ou seccionado por engano quando se liga a artéria uterina.

cards.front: Which veins drain into the left renal vein, and where do the same veins drain on the right?
cards.back: The **left gonadal vein** and **left adrenal (suprarenal) vein** drain into the left renal vein. Right-sided veins drain directly into the **IVC**. The left renal vein is longer: it crosses **in front of the aorta**, **between the aorta and the SMA**.
cards.back_pt: A **veia gonadal esquerda** e a **veia adrenal (suprarrenal) esquerda** drenam para a veia renal esquerda. À direita, ambas drenam diretamente na **VCI**. A veia renal esquerda é mais longa porque cruza **à frente da aorta**, passando **entre a aorta e a AMS**.

cards.front: Which cells form the juxtaglomerular apparatus, and what does each one do?
cards.back: **Macula densa** (end of the thick ascending limb): senses **NaCl** in the tubular fluid. **Juxtaglomerular cells** (modified smooth muscle of the **afferent arteriole**): secrete **renin**. **Extraglomerular mesangial cells**: support and help signal between them.
cards.back_pt: **Mácula densa** (final do ramo ascendente espesso): detecta o **NaCl** no líquido tubular. **Células justaglomerulares** (músculo liso modificado da **arteríola aferente**): secretam **renina**. **Células mesangiais extraglomerulares**: dão suporte e ajudam na sinalização entre elas.

cards.front: What are the urachal remnants, and how does each one present?
cards.back: **Patent urachus**: urine leaks from the **umbilicus**. **Urachal cyst**: a fluid-filled mass between umbilicus and bladder that can become infected. **Vesicourachal diverticulum**: an outpouching at the **bladder dome**. Remnants can give rise to bladder **adenocarcinoma**.
cards.back_pt: **Úraco pérvio**: saída de urina pelo **umbigo**. **Cisto do úraco**: massa com líquido entre o umbigo e a bexiga, que pode infectar. **Divertículo vesicouracal**: projeção para fora na **cúpula vesical**. Os remanescentes podem originar **adenocarcinoma** de bexiga.

questions.stem: A male newborn has severe respiratory distress soon after birth and dies within hours. Prenatal ultrasound had shown almost no amniotic fluid. On exam he has a flattened nose, a recessed chin, low-set ears, and clubbed feet. Autopsy shows small lungs, no kidneys and no ureters on either side, and a small, empty bladder. Which embryologic failure best explains these findings?
choices: Persistent mucosal folds in the posterior urethra
Fusion of the lower poles of the developing kidneys
Failure of the allantois to close
Failure of the ureteric bud to form
Incomplete canalization of the ureteropelvic junction
questions.explanation: This is **Potter sequence** from **bilateral renal agenesis**. If the **ureteric bud** does not form, it cannot induce the metanephric mesenchyme, so no ureter or kidney develops. With no fetal urine there is **oligohydramnios**, which compresses the fetus (face and limb deformities) and causes **pulmonary hypoplasia**. **Posterior urethral valves** also cause oligohydramnios, but the kidneys are present with hydronephrosis and the bladder is distended.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **sequência de Potter** por **agenesia renal bilateral**. Se o **broto ureteral** não se forma, ele não induz o mesênquima metanéfrico, e nenhum ureter ou rim se desenvolve. Sem urina fetal ocorre **oligoidrâmnio**, que comprime o feto (deformidades da face e dos membros) e causa **hipoplasia pulmonar**. As **válvulas de uretra posterior** também causam oligoidrâmnio, mas os rins estão presentes, com hidronefrose, e a bexiga fica distendida.

questions.stem: A 15-year-old girl is evaluated for short stature and no breast development. She has a webbed neck, a broad chest with widely spaced nipples, and a low hairline at the back of the neck. Her karyotype is 45,X. Abdominal ultrasound shows both kidneys joined at their lower poles and located lower in the abdomen than normal. Which structure prevented the normal ascent of her kidneys?
questions.explanation: **Turner syndrome** (45,X) is associated with **horseshoe kidney**. The kidneys normally rise from the pelvis to the lumbar region. When the lower poles fuse, the joined kidney catches on the **inferior mesenteric artery** and stays low. The **superior mesenteric artery** arises higher up; it is the vessel that compresses the left renal vein in nutcracker syndrome, not the one that blocks ascent.
questions.explanation_pt: A **síndrome de Turner** (45,X) está associada ao **rim em ferradura**. Os rins normalmente sobem da pelve até a região lombar. Quando os polos inferiores se fundem, o rim unido fica preso na **artéria mesentérica inferior** e permanece baixo. A **artéria mesentérica superior** se origina mais acima; é o vaso que comprime a veia renal esquerda na síndrome de quebra-nozes (*nutcracker*), e não o que bloqueia a subida.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old man has sudden, severe, colicky pain that began in his left flank and now spreads to his left groin and scrotum. He cannot find a comfortable position. He has no fever. Urinalysis shows blood but no white cells or nitrites. Noncontrast CT shows a 5-mm stone in the left ureter with mild hydronephrosis above it. At which site do ureteral stones most often become lodged?
choices: Crossing of the iliac vessels at the pelvic brim
questions.explanation: The **ureterovesical junction**, where the ureter passes obliquely through the bladder wall, is the **narrowest** part of the ureter and the most common site for a stone to lodge. Pain that moves from the flank toward the **groin and scrotum** fits a stone moving down the ureter. The **ureteropelvic junction** and the **pelvic brim** are also narrow points, but stones lodge there less often than at the ureterovesical junction.
questions.explanation_pt: A **junção ureterovesical**, onde o ureter atravessa obliquamente a parede da bexiga, é o ponto **mais estreito** do ureter e o local mais comum de impactação de cálculos. A dor que migra do flanco para a **região inguinal e o escroto** é compatível com um cálculo descendo pelo ureter. A **junção ureteropélvica** e a **borda da pelve** também são pontos de estreitamento, mas os cálculos ficam presos ali com menos frequência que na junção ureterovesical.

questions.stem: A 24-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after a motorcycle crash. Pelvic x-ray shows fractures of both superior and inferior pubic rami. There is blood at the urethral meatus, and he cannot urinate even though he feels the urge. On rectal exam, the prostate is high-riding and hard to feel. Which part of the urethra is most likely injured?
questions.explanation: A **pelvic fracture** shears the **posterior urethra** at the **membranous urethra**, the thin, fixed segment that passes through the urogenital diaphragm. Blood at the meatus, urinary retention and a **high-riding prostate** are the classic signs; a retrograde urethrogram is done before any catheter is placed. The **prostatic urethra** is protected inside the prostate, which moves up as one piece with the bladder. Injury of the **bulbar urethra** (anterior urethra) is typical of a **straddle injury**, not a pelvic fracture.
questions.explanation_pt: A **fratura de pelve** rompe a **uretra posterior** na **uretra membranosa**, o segmento fino e fixo que atravessa o diafragma urogenital. Sangue no meato, retenção urinária e **próstata elevada** (*high-riding prostate*) ao toque retal são os sinais clássicos; faz-se uretrografia retrógrada antes de passar qualquer sonda. A **uretra prostática** fica protegida dentro da próstata, que se desloca para cima junto com a bexiga. A lesão da **uretra bulbar** (uretra anterior) é típica da **queda a cavaleiro** (*straddle injury*), e não da fratura de pelve.

notes.title: Kidney and urinary tract: development, anatomy and histology
notes.body_md:
## Development

- Three stages: **pronephros** (disappears), **mesonephros** (temporary kidney; its duct forms male genital ducts) and **metanephros** (the permanent kidney).
- **Ureteric bud** forms the ureter, pelvis, calyces and **collecting ducts**. **Metanephric mesenchyme** forms the nephron up to the distal convoluted tubule.
- No ureteric bud means **renal agenesis**. Bilateral agenesis leads to **oligohydramnios** and **Potter sequence**: pulmonary hypoplasia, flat face, limb deformities.
- **Multicystic dysplastic kidney**: bud-mesenchyme interaction fails; a nonfunctional cystic kidney, usually unilateral.

## Position and drainage problems

- **Horseshoe kidney**: fused lower poles caught under the **inferior mesenteric artery**; linked to **Turner syndrome**.
- **Pelvic kidney**: a kidney that fails to ascend.
- **UPJ obstruction**: a common cause of hydronephrosis in fetuses and infants.

## Ureter and vessels

- Narrowings: **UPJ**, **iliac vessel crossing**, **UVJ** (narrowest).
- **Water under the bridge**: ureter runs under the uterine artery and the ductus deferens.
- Arterial path: **renal → segmental → interlobar → arcuate → interlobular → afferent arteriole**.
- **Left renal vein** is longer, crosses in front of the aorta (between the aorta and the SMA), and receives the left gonadal and left adrenal veins.

## Histology

- **Filtration barrier**: fenestrated endothelium, **glomerular basement membrane** (negatively charged), and **podocyte foot processes**.
- **Mesangial cells** support the capillary loops.
- **Juxtaglomerular apparatus**: macula densa (senses NaCl), JG cells (renin), extraglomerular mesangial cells.

## Bladder and urethra

- The **urachus** (from the allantois) should close into the median umbilical ligament. Remnants: patent urachus, urachal cyst, vesicourachal diverticulum.
- **Pelvic fracture**: posterior urethra tear at the **membranous urethra**; high-riding prostate.
- **Straddle injury**: anterior urethra tear at the **bulbar urethra**.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Desenvolvimento

- Três estágios: **pronefro** (desaparece), **mesonefro** (rim temporário; seu ducto forma os ductos genitais masculinos) e **metanefro** (o rim definitivo).
- O **broto ureteral** forma o ureter, a pelve, os cálices e os **ductos coletores**. O **mesênquima metanéfrico** forma o néfron até o túbulo contorcido distal.
- Sem broto ureteral ocorre **agenesia renal**. A agenesia bilateral leva a **oligoidrâmnio** e **sequência de Potter**: hipoplasia pulmonar, face achatada, deformidades dos membros.
- **Rim displásico multicístico**: falha na interação broto-mesênquima; rim cístico sem função, geralmente unilateral.

## Problemas de posição e de drenagem

- **Rim em ferradura**: polos inferiores fundidos presos abaixo da **artéria mesentérica inferior**; associado à **síndrome de Turner**.
- **Rim pélvico**: rim que não sobe.
- **Obstrução da JUP**: causa comum de hidronefrose em fetos e lactentes.

## Ureter e vasos

- Estreitamentos: **JUP**, **cruzamento dos vasos ilíacos**, **JUV** (o mais estreito).
- **Água sob a ponte** (*water under the bridge*): o ureter passa sob a artéria uterina e o ducto deferente.
- Trajeto arterial: **renal → segmentar → interlobar → arqueada → interlobular → arteríola aferente**.
- A **veia renal esquerda** é mais longa, cruza à frente da aorta (entre a aorta e a AMS) e recebe as veias gonadal e adrenal esquerdas.

## Histologia

- **Barreira de filtração**: endotélio fenestrado, **membrana basal glomerular** (com carga negativa) e **pedicelos dos podócitos**.
- As **células mesangiais** dão suporte às alças capilares.
- **Aparelho justaglomerular**: mácula densa (detecta NaCl), células JG (renina), células mesangiais extraglomerulares.

## Bexiga e uretra

- O **úraco** (derivado do alantoide) deve se fechar e formar o ligamento umbilical mediano. Remanescentes: úraco pérvio, cisto do úraco, divertículo vesicouracal.
- **Fratura de pelve**: lesão da uretra posterior na **uretra membranosa**; próstata elevada.
- **Queda a cavaleiro**: lesão da uretra anterior na **uretra bulbar**.
